priceSnapshot.note: Up 1,255.7 points and 1.64 percent on 24 hours against the 76,779.4 open, but DOWN 818.5 points and 1.04 percent against the 78,853.6 midday mark. The shape of the afternoon is the story. The midday add gate at 78,993.9 fired cleanly and ran: the 18:00Z bar closed 79,222.1 and price printed 79,600 on the 20:00Z bar, 746.4 points above the midday mark and the highest trade since 11 September. Then it gave all of it back and more, in five consecutive lower hourly closes - 79,101.8, 78,767.9, 78,557.6, 78,195.7 and the live 00:00Z bar at 77,981.9. Price now sits 1,564.9 points beneath the high and 98.3 points beneath the 1H EMA200 at 78,133.4, the same average that the midday report named as its reduce level at 78,029.5. The day still settled well: the 14 September 1Dutc candle CLOSED at 78,195.7, the best daily close since 09 September and 1,060.6 points above the 1Dutc EMA20. The problem is everything underneath it.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below 77,900.0, the measured long-liquidation magnet and 135.1 points under the mark. This is not an estimate: 783,163 USD of longs were force-sold in that bucket across just 8 fills in the last 90 minutes, the largest single cluster the feed has shown in three days. A settled close beneath the price where that flush already happened means the bid that absorbed it has gone, and the next measured shelf is the 77,772.4 1H EMA100 with nothing verified between there and the 77,135.1 daily average. Cut the remaining discretionary spot sleeve on that close and leave only the long-term core.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above 78,323.2, the 1H EMA20, 288.1 points above the mark. Set deliberately above the 78,133.4 EMA200 rather than at it, because reclaiming one average after a 1,564.9-point reversal is noise and reclaiming both is structure. Price has to close back through the level it broke down from AND through the faster average that has been falling all evening. That would say the evening fade was a liquidation event rather than a turn, and it would reopen 78,563.7 and the 79,101.8 shelf.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from ADD to REDUCE, one bar early and on purpose. The midday report wrote its own exit in plain terms: trim the 15.00 USDT tranche on a settled 1H close below 78,029.5. That close has NOT settled - the last settled hourly close is 78,195.7, 166.2 points above the level - so on the letter of the gate nothing has fired. It is being acted on anyway because there is no session between now and roughly 02:00 COT tomorrow, the live hourly bar is trading 47.2 points beneath the trigger with 23 minutes left to settle, and the thing that would make waiting cheap - a two-sided book - is not there. The reduce level falls 129.5 points from 78,029.5 to 77,900.0 and is now anchored to measured liquidation data rather than to a moving average. The add level falls 670.7 points from 78,993.9 to 78,323.2. The invalidation rises 111.6 points from 77,023.5 to 77,135.1 as the 1Dutc EMA20 climbs. A resting stop is RECOMMENDED for the first time in four sessions, at 77,700.0.

overnightRisk: Three specific things, in order of how much they can move price before the next report at roughly 02:00 COT. First, the FOMC decision on Wednesday 16 September with the market pricing a rate HIKE rather than a cut - rate-hike odds went above 85 percent on Friday's CPI print, the US 10-year has backed up to 4.992 percent from 4.959 at midday, and the DXY has firmed to 99.541. A hawkish repricing overnight in Asian hours hits the most crowded side of this book directly. Second, the positioning itself: open interest has collapsed 4.88 percent since midday, from 2,161,318,089 to 2,055,912,362 USD, on 1,598,366 USD of 100-percent one-sided LONG liquidations in the last 90 minutes alone, and yet the OKX long-short account ratio has gone UP through the flush, 1.20 to 1.21 to 1.22. Longs are being carried out and the survivors are adding. That is the configuration that gaps. Third, the liquidation magnet at 77,900 sits 135.1 points below spot into the thinnest liquidity window of the week - Asian hours on a Monday night - with the next verified shelf 262.7 points lower at the 77,772.4 1H EMA100. A 2.81 percent daily ATR is 2,196 points; a move of only one third of that overnight puts price through the magnet, through the EMA100 and into the 77,135.1 invalidation. The resting stop at 77,700.0 is the only protection between here and 02:00, and it is placed deliberately BELOW the 77,900 cluster so the magnet itself does not fill it. Set against all that, the constructive case is real and should not be dismissed: the day closed at 78,195.7, the best 1Dutc close since 09 September, the 4H MACD line crossed above zero for the first time since 09 September, and the first partial US spot ETF print in three sessions is POSITIVE at plus 9.7 million. If the overnight holds 77,900 the daily structure survives intact.

liquidation.note: 783,163 USD across only 8 fills - LONG liquidations, sell-side, and by a wide margin the largest cluster in the window. Eight fills for 783,163 USD means one or two very large positions were carried out at once, not a retail cascade; the single biggest print is 1,000 contracts at 77,934.4. This is the exact inverse of the midday report's 78,900 bucket, which was 438,650 USD of SHORT liquidations across 77 fills. Six hours later the same book is emptying in the opposite direction with far bigger tickets.

385,791 USD across 30 fills - long liquidations 64.9 points above the mark, sitting right on the 78,133.4 1H EMA200. This is where the breakdown through the average was paid for. Read it as spent fuel: the leverage that was defending the EMA200 has already been removed.

liquidityMagnet.note: The pull reads down and, unlike midday, the supporting data agrees rather than contradicting it. All 100 fills the feed returned are sell-side LONG liquidations totalling 1,598,366 USD with ZERO short liquidations anywhere in the 23:06:37Z to 00:36:21Z window, newest fill 15 seconds before the mark. Open interest is 2,055,912,361.89 USD, DOWN 4.88 percent from the 2,161,318,089.08 midday read - roughly 105 million USD of notional removed in six hours, and far larger than the 0.37 percent drift midday flagged. Funding has collapsed to 0.00322 percent per 8 hours, about 3.53 percent annualised, from 0.00626 percent at midday: nobody is paying to be long. The one number that does NOT confirm a completed flush is the long-short account ratio, which has risen through it - 1.20 at 22:00Z, 1.21 at 23:00Z, 1.22 at 00:00Z. The 13 September midnight lesson says a one-sided flush on falling open interest is an emptied book and therefore a reversal setup rather than a continuation, and that lesson has now been right twice. The reason it is NOT being leaned on tonight is that ratio: in both prior cases the crowded side was being genuinely reduced, whereas here accounts are net adding to longs while longs are the side being liquidated. An emptied book that refills itself on the same side is not emptied. There is also a smaller 134,126 USD long cluster at 78,000 between the mark and the 77,900 magnet, so the first 135 points down are not clean air.

indices.bias: Settled closes are in and the midday report's call was wrong. Midday saw QQQ at 712.57 intraday, argued the morning oil-shock gap had been absorbed rather than repriced, and kept the zone at fair. QQQ then faded into the bell and closed 709.18, down 5.70 and 0.80 percent, near the bottom of a 702.74 to 712.95 range - the third consecutive lower close and enough to drop it from the 33rd percentile of its trailing month to the 12th. The zone moves from fair to CHEAP. The mechanical driver is back where the morning left it: Brent has recovered to 107.00, up 1.25 percent and 1.19 percent above the 105.74 midday read, and the US 10-year has backed up to 4.992 percent from 4.959, so the two things that let tech rally at lunchtime both reversed by the close. With rate-hike odds above 85 percent into Wednesday's FOMC, a 12th-percentile print two days before the decision is a genuine monthly-DCA opportunity rather than a falling knife - but it is a monthly contribution, not a trade, and there is no reason to front-run the FOMC by a day. Wait for Wednesday.

VOO stays the larger of the two US sleeves and, like QQQ, the sensible action is to let Wednesday happen first.

Hold the existing Japan allocation, skip the discretionary top-up, and if a rebalance is wanted the direction is obvious: the cheap sleeves are the US ones.

Discretionary calls over the same six: 4 green, 2 red. Adding this session's resolution makes it 4 green and 3 red, ending a run of three consecutive green calls.
calibration.note: The midday 78,029.5 reduce gate did NOT fire on its own terms and the distinction is fine enough to be worth stating precisely. It required a settled 1H close; the lowest settled close after the 12:46 COT mark is 78,195.7 on the 23:00Z bar, 166.2 points above the level, and the live 00:00Z bar is trading 77,981.9 with 23 minutes to settle. So the gate is unfired on closes and breached on price, exactly the pattern that cost the 13 September midday session money. The 78,993.9 add gate DID fire and fired well: the 18:00Z bar closed 79,222.1, clearing by 228.2 points, and the 19:00Z and 20:00Z bars closed 78,996.7 and 79,101.8 without a retrace beneath the trigger, against a 79,600.0 high. The 77,023.5 invalidation was never approached, the session low of 77,972.8 holding 949.3 points above it. No resting stop was recommended and none would have filled. Midday published OUTRIGHT BULLISH at 42 percent with bearish at 21 - the most directional call in six sessions - and price is 818.5 points and 1.04 percent LOWER, so the headline call was wrong. Discretionary: midday ADDED a 15.00 USDT spot tranche at 78,853.6; spot marks 78,035.1, so that tranche is 818.5 points and 1.04 percent offside, roughly minus 0.16 USDT, and the whole 177.10 USDT book is now within 0.05 USDT of its cost basis. Hence false. What midday got right was the gate design - it set the add at the 24-hour high rather than under it, demanded real bid after the squeeze, and got 746.4 points of follow-through. What it got wrong is written verbatim in its own liquidityMagnet note: it observed that price rising on FALLING open interest is shorts closing rather than longs opening, called the 78,900 and 79,000 clusters spent fuel, cited the 13 September midday loss as the precedent - and then added anyway, on the reasoning that the gate had been honoured. Honouring a gate is not the same as the gate being right. Open interest has since fallen another 4.88 percent and 1,598,366 USD of longs have been liquidated. This is the third time in four days the desk has named the correct counterweight in the report and sized against it in the wallet.
